study_design: Hospital-based case-control study with prostate cancer cases and two matched control series
cohort_total_n_excerpt: One hundred patients with prostate cancer and two different control series [100 benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) patients and 100 general hospital patients] were matched to each other upon hospital admittance, age (+/- 3 years) and date of admission (+/- 3 months), and directly interviewed during admission from 1981 to 1984 in Kyoto, Japan.
reason: This case-control study evaluates dietary associations with general prostate cancer using 100 cases and two control series. No stage, grade, advanced, metastatic, lethal, or other aggressive endpoint is reported.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Total energy intake and the dietary intake of fat, protein, carbohydrate, water, fiber, ash, such vitamins as retinol, B1, B2, C, and niacin, and such minerals as calcium, potassium, sodium, phosphorus, and iron were not linked with prostate cancer risk.
estimate_classifications.reason: The abstract explicitly evaluates dietary iron in relation to general prostate cancer risk and reports no association.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: beta-Carotene as well as vitamin A contained in green/yellow vegetables were significantly protective, and those in seaweeds and kelp suggestively protective.
estimate_classifications.reason: Kelp-derived beta-carotene and vitamin A were evaluated as protective dietary factors in this general prostate cancer case-control study; no aggressive subtype is specified.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: The corresponding relative risk obtained from the vitamin A analyses was 2.82 (1.30-6.14), 2.64 (1.24-5.60), and 3.29 (1.47-7.35) in due order in the comparison with BPH patients; 2.69 (1.22-5.94), 4.78 (1.98-11.52), and 3.50 (1.52-8.06) in the comparison with hospital controls.
estimate_classifications.reason: The vitamin A relative risks concern general prostate cancer cases. The existing row is the inverse orientation of the abstract's lowest-versus-highest comparison, but its endpoint remains general.
